name: Spectrum bars
summary: The classic analyser: a row of spectrum bars with falling peak caps, solid, LED segments or outlines, mirrored or not.
credit: The classic graphic equaliser and LED spectrum analyser. Written new with Claude Code.
hint: One bar per slice of the spectrum, lows on the left (or in the middle, mirrored). Bars rise with their slice and fall at Fall; the caps hold the last peak for Hold, then drop. Tilt lifts the highs, which are quieter in most music.

params.label: Frequency axis
params.help: Log gives each octave the same width, as ears hear it; linear gives each hertz the same width, the highs spread wide.

params.label: Layout
params.help: Bottom: bars stand on the floor. Mirrored: they grow up and down from the middle line. Middle out: the lows in the middle, mirrored left and right.

params.label: Width
params.help: How much of the frame's width the row of bars takes.

params.label: Segments
params.help: With Segments: how many LED cells a full bar has.

params.label: Colour by
params.help: Height: the palette runs up each bar, like a meter. Position: across the row, lows to highs. One colour: the layer's colour.

params.label: Reflection
params.help: With Bottom: the bars mirrored faintly in the floor.

params.label: Range
params.help: How far below the loudest slice the bars reach: more shows more of the quiet. The loudest is followed over a few seconds, so any track fills the row.

params.label: Tilt
params.help: Lifts the highs (up to 4.5 dB an octave), which are quieter in most music, so the row looks level.

params.label: Fall
params.help: How fast a bar falls, in full heights a second.

params.label: Hold
params.help: How long a peak cap stays before it drops.
